leading_positions.synthesis: Six members list the optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) in their round-1 preferred configuration, five of them as the sole prize part and Johansson as one of two parts. Shared: the magic-wavelength lattice as a distinct invention, performance near 1e-18 reproduced and surpassed by independent laboratories, and a two-name credit divided between concept (Katori) and performance (Ye). Not shared: Johansson would add a second, unrelated part (B037); several supporters (Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce) say priority between concept and performance is recalled from general knowledge and not verified; Danielsson, Mehlig and Kroll want the citation to name the lattice clock specifically and not optical clocks or precision spectroscopy generally; Danielsson would keep the SI redefinition of the second out of the citation. Note that the chair is among these supporters.

Two members prefer topological insulators (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) as the sole prize part, and B007 is the only candidate that all eight members ranked in their opening top four, as Eriksson and Olsson note. Shared by these two: the Z2 invariant and quantum spin Hall state as a new organising principle, a stable interpretation over about two decades, and a clean theory-to-measurement chain through the HgTe edge-conductance result. Not shared: Eriksson would keep the citation centred on the concept and accept the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap as a regrettable unfairness, while Olsson says that if the HgTe proposal is judged indispensable the three-name limit cannot give a fair attribution. Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce each list B007 as an alternative and not a preferred prize.

A single member proposes a two-part prize pairing the lattice clock (Katori, Ye) with Hosono for iron-based high-temperature superconductors, using exactly three names. Johansson argues that both have unambiguous attribution and are mature, and that the open pairing mechanism is an interpretation gap and not a gap in the discovery. Johansson also concedes that the two parts have almost nothing in common, that Hosono has thin support among colleagues, and that a sole-laureate share in a field with rapid multi-group follow-up may look unbalanced. No other member's configuration includes B037, and no other member addresses it in the files.

areas_of_agreement: No member ranks any candidate as scientifically weak. Both leading single-achievement candidates, B056 and B007, are described by supporters and critics alike as mature with a stable interpretation.

All eight configurations name either B056 (six members) or B007 (two members) as the lead, and every member lists at least one of these two among their preferred configuration or alternatives. Six of eight list B007 as an alternative.
Members who comment on B056 name the same two laureates, Katori and Ye, and nobody proposes a different pair or a third name for it.

No member's preferred configuration includes B012, B003, B058 or B018. B012 is an alternative for Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson (and was Danielsson's opening first choice), and several members describe B012 and B058 as better suited to a later year rather than excluding them in principle.

Several members agree that the citation for any metrology prize should name the lattice clock explicitly, and that for B007 it should state the Z2/time-reversal-symmetric mechanism so that novelty relative to the 2016 prize is clear.
Members place weight on discovery or invention with clearly identifiable originators and on independent reproduction, and say they reason from the science and not from opening vote counts.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a distinct invention or an incremental step after the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce argue that the combs are a readout tool and ion control a different regime, whereas the lattice clock removes the trapping Stark shift and allows many neutral atoms to be interrogated at once. Olsson argues the clock refines an existing timekeeping capability and that topological insulators opened a materials class and conceptual framework.

Whether the 2016 prize for topological phases and phase transitions leaves room for B007. Eriksson, Olsson and Lindroth say Z2 classification with time-reversal-symmetric helical edges is a different step from the quantum Hall and Haldane lineage honoured in 2016; Danielsson says Kane-Mele extends that conceptual line and so is somewhat less original; Mehlig opened with the concern that the earlier prize may make the committee reluctant, and others flag the overlap as an open judgement.

Whether B007 or B056 has the greater scientific consequence. Olsson and Eriksson weight impact on electronic matter and first-principles analysis, while Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce weight measurable consequences such as 1e-18 clocks, relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and the redefinition of the second.

Whether the pairing mechanism in B037 and in B012 is an interpretation gap or an obstacle. Johansson treats the open iron-based pairing mechanism as an interpretation gap with a settled discovery, while Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce treat the open pairing mechanism and sample-dependent phase diagram in B012 as grounds to wait.

Whether the closeness of circuit QED (B058) to the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits is a bar. Johansson, Kroll and Mehlig raise it; Mehlig adds that the platform is still evolving quickly.
attribution_disputes: B007: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe as the platform and the experiment followed their proposal; Zhang died in 2018, and the three-dimensional topological insulator work of Fu, Moore, Balents, Hasan and others also sits outside the three names. Members differ on whether the BHZ proposal was indispensable to the Molenkamp observation (Olsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson, Mehlig, Pearce, Danielsson treat it as a serious credit defect; Eriksson treats it as regrettable but not disqualifying because the concept and invariant are Kane and Mele's).

B056: Ludlow, Lemonde, Oates and other lattice-clock and ion-clock groups are not among the credited names. Danielsson, Lindroth and Mehlig note the gap but argue it is the normal long tail of a prize; Kroll, Mehlig and Pearce say widening to a third name is not supported by the evidence. Kroll and Lindroth add that the split between Katori's concept and Ye's performance is partly intertwined historically, and several members state they are recalling priority from general knowledge.

B003: Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth, in responding to Pearce's opening position, say two names (Halzen, Karle) cannot honestly represent a very large collaboration or the AMANDA and DUMAND predecessors, and ask which contributions by Halzen and Karle were decisive for the discovery as distinct from construction. Pearce accepts the collaboration-credit criticism in his round-1 statement.

B012: Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce point out that early experimental credit is shared among Cao, Jarillo-Herrero and other groups (Dean, Young, Yacoby) and that earlier twisted-bilayer band-flattening theory is not captured by the credited names.

B018: Mehlig notes that the Jaksch-Zoller proposal, the superfluid-to-Mott experiment and the quantum-gas microscope are separable steps and that later microscope work is by others, so the decisive prize-worthy step is arguable.
maturity_disputes: B012: Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce and Johansson regard the interpretation as still moving, with superconductivity and the phase diagram debated and the experimental form under a decade old; Danielsson ranked it first at opening and treats the field as timely.
B003: Lindroth and Kroll describe source identification of the astrophysical neutrino flux as on the edge of premature, and Pearce notes the origin of the diffuse flux is unresolved.

B056: whether the pending SI redefinition of the second is evidence of maturity, a coincident timing factor, or a reason to wait. Danielsson, Mehlig and Pearce say the physics is already settled and the redefinition is a consequence and not a reason, while Lindroth and Kroll record that metrology prizes may be held back until the redefinition concludes.
B037: Johansson says the discovery is nearly two decades old and well replicated, so its unresolved mechanism is not a maturity bar; no other member comments on this.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: possible recusal issue for B058 (circuit QED) and any other superconducting-circuit candidate; works on circuit and waveguide QED, directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology at Chalmers, has Chalmers colleagues Delsing and Wilson, and ranked B058 first at opening. Johansson reports no specific connection to B056, B037, B007 or B012.

Kroll: documented research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder during doctoral work; Hall belongs to the 2005 frequency-comb background of the lattice-clock field. Kroll reports no documented relationship with Katori or Ye and sees no specific recusal trigger.

Pearce (chair): documented astroparticle and gamma-ray instrumentation experience (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO+) is adjacent to B003, which Pearce listed as an alternative; no IceCube membership or personal tie is recorded. Pearce also supports B056 as the preferred configuration, so the chair is a participant on the leading position as well as the summariser.

Eriksson, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson report no specific conflict. Eriksson discloses professional proximity to condensed-matter candidates such as B007, and Lindroth discloses atomic-physics community proximity to B056, both without a recusal trigger. Olsson notes a shared Chalmers affiliation with Johansson that is not a connection to any shortlisted candidate. Danielsson reports no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: For B056: does the committee accept that the lattice clock is distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and can members who doubt this say what additional distinction in the citation would resolve it?

For B056: can the committee verify, from documented sources and not recollection, the priority sequence between Katori's magic-wavelength concept and the first lattice-clock demonstrations, and is the two-name credit to Katori and Ye still defensible after considering Ludlow, Lemonde, Oates and other groups?

For B007: was the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal indispensable to the Molenkamp HgTe observation, and if so can any citation wording or three-name configuration be fair given Zhang's death and the three-dimensional topological insulator work?

For B007: given the 2016 prize, what specific wording of the citation would make the novelty of the Z2 invariant and time-reversal-symmetric helical edge states explicit, and do members who place B007 as an alternative regard that wording as sufficient to move it up?

Does the committee prefer a single-achievement prize (B056 or B007) to a two-part combination such as B056 with B037, and if a second part is considered, which candidate beyond B037 would members support within a three-name limit?
Should the pending SI redefinition of the second count as evidence of maturity for B056, be treated as coincident, or be a reason to wait, and should the citation mention it?

For B003, B012 and B058: does any member wish to bring these forward this year, and if so what specific evidence (decisive contributions of Halzen and Karle, settled pairing mechanism, distance from the 2025 prize) would change the maturity or attribution objections raised in round 1?
Is any recusal or abstention advised in light of the disclosed flags, in particular Johansson on B058 and Kroll's connection to the Hall laboratory on B056?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows two substantive centres of gravity. B056 (Katori, Ye) is the sole or lead configuration for six members and has the cleanest credit in the files, but its supporters disagree on how much weight overlap with the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes and unverified priority history should carry. B007 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is preferred by two members and listed as an alternative by six, and the main open question is whether the BHZ attribution gap and the 2016 prize can be resolved by citation wording or are disqualifying. The remaining candidates are held back mainly by maturity (B012, B003) or attribution (B003, B018) objections that members raised themselves. These are counts of explicit round-1 positions only, and nothing here is a ruling.
